title: Interview eval reads a generated brief snapshot, not a hand-kept Python port
acceptance: node:test (app/_lib/voice/interview-brief-snapshot.test.ts): rendering default, student, case and grounded through the production builders with the role/title sentinel gives exactly the templates in the committed pipeline/jobfit/eval/interview_briefs.json. Comparing against a doctored copy with one changed clause fails, and the failure names the kind and the regenerate command (npm run interview:briefs).

On failure it falls back to default_brief (:293), and the row is still labelled brief='grounded' (run_golden/run_scenarios carry s.brief). pipeline/jobfit/tests/skip-register.json:29 names TestGroundedBridge.test_grounded_brief_renders_the_real_run_of_show as the one env-conditional skip. pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_interview_eval.py:575-579 skips it when the bridge is unavailable, pipeline/jobfit/tests/run_gated.py:74 pins ENV_CONDITIONAL_SKIPS = 1, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:420 carries KP_SKIP_BASELINE "5" for it.

The revert commit therefore needs one `Gate-exemption: skip-baseline-raised at .github/workflows/ci.yml — reverting the brief-snapshot series` trailer.

body:
## Summary
The voice-interviewer eval is supposed to test the brief the product ships. By default it tests a Python retyping of that brief instead: roughly 150 lines of prompt literals in interview_eval.py, held to the TS source only by a substring test. Every copy change to the interviewer brief is therefore written twice, in two languages. When the node bridges that render the real brief fail, the run falls back without a sound, and a grounded scenario ends up scored against the default brief. This card makes the production briefs a committed, generated snapshot. The TS builders emit it with a role/title sentinel, a node:test holds it to the live builders, and Python only ever reads it. The port, both subprocess bridges and the gated suite's one env-conditional skip all go away.

## Description
interview_eval.py:76-84 still carries the plan it never finished ('Phase 2 replaces this port'). Today there are three ways to get a brief. `port` is the default (:1385) and is the Python re-render. `ts` spawns node per role, with a silent fallback to the port (:259). `grounded` spawns node plus a temp DB, with a silent fallback to the DEFAULT brief (:293) while the row stays labelled grounded. The drift guard (tests/test_interview_eval.py:591-604) only checks that each Python literal still appears somewhere in student-interview.ts. That catches a TS edit only by making the Python gate red, which is why 5 of the 24 brief commits also had to touch interview_eval.py. The grounded check cannot run in the python-gate job at all (no node_modules), so it is the register's one env-conditional skip (skip-register.json:29, run_gated.py:74, ci.yml:420).

The move is the one certification-levels asks of a derived model: make it a stored derivation that names how it is rebuilt, and check it against its source. `scripts/interview-briefs-snapshot.ts` renders default, student, case and grounded through the real builders (grounded reuses the interview-brief-grounded fixture in a throwaway KP_DB_PATH). A sentinel stands where the role or title goes, and the script writes `pipeline/jobfit/eval/interview_briefs.json` (schema, kinds, templates). The node:test in test:unit re-renders and compares, and proves by direct render that substituting the sentinel is faithful. Python replaces the sentinel with str.replace and never spawns anything.

## Flow
1. Add scripts/interview-briefs-snapshot.ts, exporting `renderBriefSnapshot()`, plus `npm run interview:briefs`, which writes the JSON with LF endings. `scripts/interview-brief.ts` keeps its CLI and reuses the same render.
2. Add app/_lib/voice/interview-brief-snapshot.test.ts to cover acceptance 1-3. It sets KP_DB_PATH to a temp file before importing the db slice, and never imports the app/_lib/db.ts barrel.
3. interview_eval.py: delete the PERSONA_*/NON_NEGOTIABLES/CLOSING literals, _port_brief, _ts_brief and _grounded_brief. Add `load_brief_snapshot()`, validated at import like thresholds.py. `render_brief(scenario)` substitutes the sentinel and raises on an unknown kind. `default_brief` and `student_brief` remain as snapshot-backed wrappers. `--briefs` stays accepted for one release as a no-op that notes that the snapshot is the production text.
4. interview_optimize.py: brief_mode plumbing is dropped. Ablation patterns stay as they are, since they match the same text.
5. tests/test_interview_eval.py: TestBriefBridge, TestBriefDriftGuard and TestGroundedBridge become snapshot tests (acceptance 4-6).
6. Remove the grounded entry from skip-register.json, set ENV_CONDITIONAL_SKIPS to 0 (update test_run_gated.py's pinned default), and set ci.yml KP_SKIP_BASELINE to "4" (a lowering, which is a repair per change-review.md:80).
7. Docs: rewrite the Phase 2 paragraphs in voice-interview-testing.md and the skip-register paragraph in testing-and-evaluation.md.

## Expected impact
An interviewer-brief copy change is written once, in TS. The eval then fails only if the snapshot was not regenerated, and the regenerate command is named in the failure. Every eval mode (offline, CI, operator sim, optimizer) scores the text the live agent receives. The scenario labelled grounded is always scored against the grounded brief. The Python gate loses its only environment-dependent skip, so the suite's skip band tightens from 4-5 to exactly 4. There is no product or UI change, and the TS builders are read, never edited.

## Evaluation
Claim: the interview eval renders every brief kind from a committed snapshot that a node:test proves equal to the production builders, with no Python prompt literals and no silent fallback.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: architecture. The new node:test in `npm run test:unit`, the rewritten test_interview_eval cases in `npm run test:python:gate` (4 skips), and `npm run lint` + `npx tsc --noEmit`.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture. There is no perf-budget exposure: nothing is added to app/page.tsx or any route graph, and the new TS module is a script plus a test.

Phase 2 replaces'; :1385 'parser.add_argument("--briefs", choices=["port", "ts"], default="port",'; :259 'interview_eval: TS brief-bridge failed ({exc}); using Python port for {scenario.name}'; :293 'interview_eval: grounded bridge failed ({exc}); using default brief for {scenario.name}'. student-interview.ts:155/157/161/175/183 'export const PERSONA_GENDER_GRAMMAR / PERSONA_LANGUAGE_DETECT / PERSONA_ONE_QUESTION / PERSONA_CRAFT_CONDENSED / PERSONA_HOSTILITY'. test_interview_eval.py:591 'def test_ported_constants_match_ts_source'; :578 'self.skipTest("grounded DB-fixture bridge unavailable (node/DB)")'. skip-register.json:29 id ...TestGroundedBridge.test_grounded_brief_renders_the_real_run_of_show, when env-conditional. run_gated.py:74 'ENV_CONDITIONAL_SKIPS = 1'. ci.yml:420 'KP_SKIP_BASELINE: "5"'. git: `git log -- app/_lib/student-interview.ts app/_lib/voice/index.ts` = 24 commits, of which 5 also touch pipeline/jobfit/eval/interview_eval.py. No r08 card writes student-interview.ts, voice/index.ts, interview-run.ts or any eval file (r08 write sets checked). The one r08 file nearby, pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_interview_scenario.py, is not in this write set.

title: A stale eval record names the units that moved, not just two aggregates
acceptance: thresholds.certify_live: a deterministic bar recorded as units {a:1,b:1,c:1} (rate 1.0, n=3) and certified live as {a:1,b:1,d:1} (rate 1.0, n=3) gives exactly one finding that names 'left: c' and 'joined: d'. Today this case certifies with 0 findings, because value and n both match.

thresholds.certify_live: MATCHING_THRESHOLDS.role_relevance_at5 recorded as {s1:1.0, s2:0.6} and live as {s1:0.8, s2:0.8} has the same mean and the same n, and gives a finding that names 's1 1.0 -> 0.8' and 's2 0.6 -> 0.8'.
thresholds.certify_live: live units identical to the record give []. A finding lists at most 10 changed units, then '+k more', and always ends with the bar's recorder command.

thresholds.record_measurements: writes measurements.units.json with one unit per line, sorted by bar and then by unit id. Recording the same run twice leaves both files byte-identical. A --record run in CI is still refused (record_refusal unchanged).

thresholds: a live unit map carrying a duplicate id raises ValueError naming the id. At load, a deterministic bar with a measurements.json record but no units entry raises a ValueError that names its recorder command (the same shape as bind_measurements:328-331).

each eval's live_units(): matching gives one '<scenario>' unit per scenario for archetype_accuracy and role_relevance_at5, and one per early-career scenario for entry_precision. automation --no-llm gives '<task>/<scenario>'. fault gives '<mode>/<task>/<scenario>'. intake --no-llm gives '<persona>/<check>'. For every bar the unit count equals the n that live_measurements reports, and the ids are unique.

`npm run test:eval:ci` exits 0 on the tree after `--record` has been run once per eval, and exits 1 with a units finding when one intake persona's check is renamed in intake_scenarios.json while another persona gains one (net n unchanged).
premise: pipeline/jobfit/eval/thresholds.py:444-467: certify_live compares only the rounded rate and the count n of each deterministic bar. The identity of the units behind them is never read.

pipeline/jobfit/eval/thresholds.py:461-466: a stale record asks the operator to decide 'if the change is intended, re-record ... if it is not, the engine regressed', and gives them only 'live X over n=N, recorded Y over n=M'. That is a blind decision the run holds the data for.

pipeline/jobfit/eval/matching_eval.py:425 averages per-scenario role_relevance_at5, and matching_eval.py:447-459 hands certify_live only that mean. One scenario losing relevance while another gains the same amount certifies clean.

pipeline/jobfit/eval/intake_eval.py:292-298: the docstring says that a scenario that 'silently lost a key (and with it an assertion) moves n'. But n is only the check total summed at intake_eval.py:268, so a lost check paired with a check added elsewhere leaves n at 98 and certifies.

pipeline/jobfit/eval/fault_eval.py:606-610 makes the same claim ('a seam or task that silently left the matrix moves n'), over 240 drill rows (measurements.json FAULT_THRESHOLD n=240). A swapped row keeps n.
pipeline/jobfit/eval/automation_eval.py:322-326 certifies RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD as (reliability, total) over 42 task-runs. The rows already carry task and scenario (automation_eval.py:488).

pipeline/jobfit/eval/thresholds.py:470-486 renders measurements.json one line per bar, so a --record diff shows the reviewer that a number moved but never which scenarios, checks or drill rows the new record accepts.
rollback: Purely additive. certify_live gains a units comparison and the files gain one sibling JSON. Reverting the series removes measurements.units.json and the units code paths. measurements.json is untouched in shape (schema 1), so the r04 certification keeps working unchanged after the revert.
runner_up: Give the voice interviewer its own reliability bar and 13-of-13 golden coverage, then gate interview_eval --no-llm --strict in CI. This adopts the deferred 'Add interview_eval --no-llm --strict to test:eval:ci'. Today interview_eval.py:65 borrows automation's RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD (n=42 task-runs), and interview_golden.json covers only swe_senior_strong and adversarial_asks_score.
body:
## Summary
When a keyless eval's certified record goes stale, the operator gets two numbers and one question: was this intended, or did the engine regress? The run already knows the answer's ingredients, namely which scenario, check or drill row changed. This card records each deterministic bar's units by identity next to the aggregate. A stale-record finding then names what left, what joined and what flipped. A --record diff also shows the reviewer exactly which units the new record accepts. The same identity check closes a real blind spot: a swapped unit keeps both rate and n, and it certifies clean today.

## Description
The r04 change made measurements recorded rather than typed, and certifies each deterministic bar as a (rate, n) pair (thresholds.py:444-467). n was chosen deliberately as the tripwire for a lost assertion (intake_eval.py:293-295, fault_eval.py:607-609). But a count cannot tell 'lost one, gained one' from 'nothing changed', and the harness's own golden path says scores attach to scenario identities (identity-survives-reuse). Matching is worse still. Relevance@5 is a mean over scenarios (matching_eval.py:425), so compensating moves are invisible. And the only operator-facing surface, the stale-record line at thresholds.py:461-466, cannot say where to look. The surface this card changes is the stderr finding that all four gated evals print through settle_live (thresholds.py:533-550), plus the `--record` summary line at :541-545. Both are rendered once, in thresholds.py, so every eval that shows the status gets the change from one place.

## Flow
1. thresholds.py: `LiveUnits = Mapping[bar, Mapping[unit_id, float]]`. Add `load_units()` and `bind_units()`: a deterministic bar must have units, the ids must be unique, and the count must equal the recorded n. `certify_live(live, units)` adds left, joined and flipped findings, capped at 10 plus '+k more' and ending with the recorder command. `record_measurements` also writes measurements.units.json (sorted, one unit per line, LF). `settle_live` passes both through.
2. Each gated eval adds `live_units(...)` beside live_measurements, built from data it already holds: matching ScenarioResult.name, automation Row task/scenario, fault Row mode/task/scenario, intake (persona, checks dict). Each main passes it to settle_live.
3. Run each `--record` locally once and commit the generated measurements.units.json (the operator act the r04 design already requires, and never in CI).
4. Tests: acceptance 1-5 in test_thresholds.py, and acceptance 6 in the automation, fault and intake eval tests plus a matching case in test_thresholds.
5. Docs: extend the bars-and-ratchets section of testing-and-evaluation.md with units, the new finding shape and the re-record review.

## Expected impact
The CI line that says a record is stale becomes something the operator can act on. It names the scenario, check or drill row, so 'intended or regression' is answered by reading 1-10 ids instead of by re-running four evals by hand and diffing their reports. A --record diff becomes reviewable per unit. The count-only hole closes: a persona check or fault seam swapped for another can no longer certify. Read cost is one extra JSON file (about 400 short lines) at import. There is no product surface, no app route and no catalog change.

## Evaluation
Claim: every deterministic eval bar is certified by unit identity as well as by rate and n, and a stale record names the units that changed.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: policy-tighten. The test_thresholds, test_automation_eval, test_fault_eval and test_intake_eval cases in `npm run test:python:gate`, and `npm run test:eval:ci` green on the recorded tree.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten. The gate gets stricter only, and a recorded tree certifies exactly as before.
evidence: thresholds.py:455 'if bar.measured is None or not _same(value, bar.measured):' and :457 'if n != bar.n:'. These are the only two comparisons certify_live makes. thresholds.py:464-465 '...if the change is intended, re-record it with `{bar.recorder}` ... if it is not, the engine regressed.' matching_eval.py:425 'rel = sum(s.role_relevance_at5 for s in self.scenarios) / n'. matching_eval.py:453-454 live = aggregate + n only. intake_eval.py:268 'checks_held = sum(sum(1 for v in c.values() if v) for _, c, _ in rows)'. intake_eval.py:293-295 docstring: 'a scenario that silently lost a key (and with it an assertion) moves ``n``'. fault_eval.py:608-609: 'so a seam or task that silently left the matrix moves ``n``'. automation_eval.py:326 'return {"RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD": (agg["reliability"], agg["total"])}'. measurements.json: FAULT n=240, INTAKE n=98, RELIABILITY n=42, matching n=7/4/7, and no per-unit data anywhere in the file. This is not a restatement of r04 'Keyless evals certify their own recorded measurement, not a hand-typed one'. That card built the (rate, n) record, and this card closes the identity gap it left. No r08 card writes any file in this set.
